advices.diagnosis: The OrderService class exhibits classic god‑class symptoms: a high number of methods (NOM=26) and total cyclomatic complexity (WMC=56) combined with very low cohesion (LCOM4=5). It bundles four distinct responsibilities—order lifecycle, pricing, audit, and notification—into a single component, which also creates a modest dependency footprint (DCC=4). The low DAM (1.0) shows all attributes are private, which is fine, but the scattered concerns drive the cohesion problem and inflate the size metrics.

suggestions.title: Extract pricing responsibilities to a dedicated PricingService in the domain layer
suggestions.sketch: Create a new class src.domain.pricing:PricingService that holds _tax_rate, _discounts and implements set_discount, discount_for, bulk_discount, set_tax_rate, apply_tax, total_for, policy_rate, is_priced. Move the corresponding methods from OrderService into this class and inject an instance via the OrderService constructor (application layer may import domain). OrderService will delegate pricing calls (e.g., self._pricing.total_for(...)).

advices.risk_notes: Introducing a new domain service adds an extra dependency; existing code that directly calls OrderService pricing methods must be updated to use the delegated interface, which could break callers if not refactored consistently. Unit tests for pricing logic need to be duplicated or redirected to the new class. If the pricing rules are tightly coupled to order lifecycle state, careful coordination is required to avoid circular imports.
